newsitem.title: POLAND: Denmark, Poland to study future Baltic energy net.
newsitem.headline: Denmark, Poland to study future Baltic energy net.

text.p: Denmark's Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen, visiting Poland on Monday, proposed the two countries launch a joint study of a future energy network linking states of the Baltic Sea region.

"I have proposed to the prime minister that we could start making a common study about the possibilities of creating a new energy network around the Baltic Sea," he said after more than two hours of talks with Polish premier Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz.
Rasmussen told a news conference the scheme would involve pooling planning and investment but gave no details, saying he did not want to pre-empt the study by experts.
He said that while any such scheme would have a commercial basis, politicians and governments should lay ambitious plans stretching 20 or 30 years into the future.
"We are talking about heavy infrastructure investments, for instance in natural gas, and that demands long-term planning," he said.
Asked whether such a scheme might lessen Polish reliance on Russian energy, Rasmussen said Russia could be included.
"Why not have a broad network covering Norway, Norwegian gas, oil, and also the whole Baltic region including Russia? Why not also try to integrate Russian energy into this new networking?" he said.

Last year Poland clinched a 25-year agreement with Russia's giant state-owned gas supplier Gazprom for the supply of 250 billion cubic metres of natural gas, but it later also expressed interest in long-term supplies of Norwegian gas.

The imports of Russian gas, through a pipeline from the Yamal Siberian peninsula, should cover between 30 and 40 percent of Poland's needs in the 1997 to 2010 period, estimated at 22 to 27 billion cubic metres per year.
Rasmussen also proposed a joint Danish-Polish study on environmental protection of the Baltic sea region.
The prime ministers signed an agreement on economic and technical grant aid from Denmark's government to Poland, to help its economic reforms and bid to join the European Union.
The amounts of the aid, in the form of expert assistance, education and technology transfer, will be set later.
Rasmussen, on the first day of his three-day official visit to Poland, expressed Danish support for Poland's admission to NATO and the EU.
The visit coincides with a Baltic region gathering of finance ministers from 10 north European states in Bergen, Norway. -- Anthony Barker +48 22 653 9700
